note: Candidates for the six reel faces. Original SVG drawings (see PROVENANCE.md). 'fact' lines are checked against park sources before the review page is sent.

creatures.name: Peninsular bighorn sheep
creatures.fact: The park's symbol; the Peninsular population was listed as federally endangered in 1998.

creatures.name: Kit fox
creatures.fact: Large ears for hearing prey and shedding heat; listed among the animals seen across the park.

creatures.name: Coyote
creatures.fact: Listed among the animals seen throughout the park.

creatures.name: Greater roadrunner
creatures.fact: Documented in the park; runs fast on the ground, which suits a race.

creatures.name: Gambel's quail
creatures.fact: Recorded in the park bird counts; the curled head plume is its signature.

creatures.name: Costa's hummingbird
creatures.fact: Recorded in the park; the male's violet gorget flares at the sides.

creatures.name: Desert pupfish
creatures.fact: The only native fish of the region and endangered; it lives naturally only in nearby San Felipe and Salt creeks. Breeding males turn bright blue.

creatures.name: Tarantula hawk wasp
creatures.fact: Common in the park; up to two inches long, it paralyzes tarantulas rather than killing them.

creatures.name: Giant desert hairy scorpion
creatures.fact: Seen year-round on warm, moonless nights.

creatures.name: Desert tarantula
creatures.fact: Three species live in the park; in fall the males wander the lower desert looking for mates.

creatures.name: Ocotillo
creatures.fact: Also a place on the old board (Ocotillo Wells).

creatures.name: Desert sand verbena
creatures.fact: Carpets the sand dunes purple in good wildflower years.

creatures.name: Beavertail cactus
creatures.fact: Flat pads with bright magenta blooms in spring.

creatures.name: Chuckwalla
creatures.fact: A big, flat-bodied lizard that wedges itself into rock crevices.

creatures.name: Sidewinder
creatures.fact: A small rattlesnake that moves sideways across loose sand.

creatures.name: Flat-tailed horned lizard
creatures.fact: A flat, spiny sand-dweller listed among the park's lizards; it hides by lying still and buries itself in loose sand.
